exact_necessity: Multiplying each activated mixed row by its integer potential and summing gives sum_a d_a z_a = sum_ab w_ab y_ab.
For Boolean selectors, 0 <= y_ab <= z_a z_b. Dropping negative w terms gives Q(z) = sum_ab max(w_ab,0) z_a z_b - sum_a d_a z_a >= 0.
Assigning each positive edge weight to either endpoint gives a necessary signed linear selector inequality because z_endpoint >= z_a z_b.
At a fixed Boolean candidate, choosing an absent endpoint whenever one exists makes the linear capacity exactly the quadratic capacity. The resulting violation is exactly -Q(candidate).
Each allocation is a globally valid necessary linear inequality. Its discovery candidate is not an incidence assumption.
